newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks sink at close on jumpy bonds, peseta.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks sink at close on jumpy bonds, peseta.

text.p: Madrid stocks sank to close with losses across all sectors on Tuesday amid instability in the currency and bond markets and other bourses.
Dealers said the volatile, jumpy mood in the markets would continue to push prices down in the short term.
The general index fell 3.78 points, 0.79 percent, to 473.15 and Ibex-35 lost 43.81 points, 0.8 percent, to 5,414.82.
"The day was similar to yesterday, although the losses were smaller, with the same expectations of short term volatility and further drops," one dealer said.
Trading volume reached a heavy 76.3 billion pesetas with nearly 40 percent of it in Telefonica and Aldolfo Dominguez.
The newly floated Aldolfo Dominguez fashion house more than doubled its purchase price at the start and then slipped 15 pesetas to settle at 5,950 with 1.7 million shares traded.

The bourse was evacuated earlier in the day because of a bomb scare, but trading was only interrupted in some small, marginal stocks until bomb-sniffing dogs searched the exchange. Screen-based trading was unaffected.
Big banks showed losses of more than one percent. Telefonica rose 10 pesetas to 3,350 in heavy trade.
